record.title: Yangzhou reports a citywide platform coordinating compute with electricity price and carbon signals
record.summary: A China Science and Technology Daily report republished by a Beijing municipal science portal says a city-level compute-electricity coordination platform entered operation in Yangzhou on Oct 28. It describes links among compute demand, green-power supply, electricity prices and hourly carbon data to help schedule flexible, non-real-time tasks. The report gives 24 connected compute pools, 16,000 PFLOPS and over 5,000 registered users. Xinhua Finance reported on Oct 27 that the platform had recently entered operation after a September trial and attributes preliminary transaction, cost and carbon figures to that trial. A July Jiangsu government report separately says an operations center was unveiled July 23 and a related compute-electricity pilot completed, but does not clarify whether it is the same system or scope. The rollout chronology and reported metrics remain unresolved and unaudited. This is a reported infrastructure rollout, not demonstrated sustained savings or general feasibility.
organizations: State Grid Yangzhou Power Supply Company

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: A government-hosted China Science and Technology Daily story and an Xinhua Finance report describe a Yangzhou compute-electricity coordination platform.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The platform links compute demand with electricity-price and hourly carbon signals and is operating at city scale in Yangzhou.

claims.label: DISPUTED
claims.text: Xinhua Finance reported on Oct 27 that the platform had recently entered operation after a September trial; the Oct 29 government-hosted article says city-level operation began Oct 28.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: Xinhua Finance attributes over RMB 1 million in matched trades, about 15% lower compute costs, and about 50% lower carbon emissions in one task-shifting scenario to the trial.

claims.label: NOT_ESTABLISHED
claims.text: The available reports establish sustained savings, sustained emissions reductions, improved compute utilization or transferability to other cities.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: A July 26 Jiangsu government report says an operations center was unveiled July 23 and that Yangzhou Big Data Group and State Grid Yangzhou had completed a compute-electricity coordination pilot.

contradictory_evidence: Xinhua Finance reported on Oct 27 that the platform had recently gone into operation after a September trial. A July 26 Jiangsu government report says an operations center was unveiled July 23 and a compute-electricity coordination pilot had been completed, but does not establish whether that work is the same system/scope. The Oct 29 report dates the city-level platform launch to Oct 28. These could be staged events, but the source record does not reconcile their identity or chronology; an operator notice is still needed.

evidence_gaps.description: Xinhua Finance's Oct 27 report describes operation after a September trial; a July Jiangsu government account reports a July 23 operations-center unveiling and a completed pilot involving the same named entities; the Oct 29 report dates city-level operation to Oct 28. Whether these are stages of one system or distinct deployments is unresolved.
No task-level dispatch or power data, metric definitions, counterfactual baseline, accounting method, transaction records or independent audit support the reported cost and carbon figures.

brief.importance_rationale: If sustained, city-scale scheduling of flexible compute against electricity price and hourly carbon signals could materially affect AI infrastructure cost, renewable-energy use and local compute operations. Current evidence is secondary reporting about a rollout and preliminary claimed figures, not audited savings or transferability.
limitations: The latest launch account is media reporting republished by a government portal; no operator technical commissioning notice was recovered.

Xinhua Finance reports a September trial, a July Jiangsu government account reports a July 23 operations-center unveiling and completed pilot, and the Oct 29 portal article dates citywide operation to Oct 28. A staged rollout is plausible, but the sources do not establish whether the earlier activity is the same system and scope.
No public task-level dispatch logs, workload eligibility rules, system architecture or carbon-accounting method were inspected.
Transaction, compute-cost and emissions figures are reported without measurement protocol, sample size, denominator, baseline or independent audit.

The Oct 29 article separately repeats one firm's 70% compute-cost reduction and 5–10x productivity claim after adopting its own model; it does not attribute those figures to the coordination platform, so they are not treated as its results.

The report gives 24 connected compute pools, 16,000 PFLOPS and over 5,000 registered users. Xinhua Finance reported on Oct 27 that the platform had recently entered operation after a September trial and attributes preliminary transaction, cost and carbon figures to that trial. A July Jiangsu government report separately says an operations center was unveiled July 23 and a related compute-electricity pilot completed, but does not clarify whether it is the same system or scope. technical.claimed_result: The Oct 29 report says citywide operation began Oct 28 and lists 24 compute-resource pools, 16,000 PFLOPS and over 5,000 registered users. Xinhua Finance's Oct 27 report says the platform had recently entered operation after a September trial, and attributes over RMB 1 million in matched trades, around 15% lower compute costs, and about 50% lower emissions in one same-task timing-shift scenario. These are reported figures, not independently audited measurements.
technical.compute_or_cost: Xinhua Finance reports more than RMB 1 million in matched trades, around 15% lower compute cost, and around 50% lower carbon emissions for one task shifted to a midday renewable-rich period. Methods, sample size and independent validation are absent.
technical.demonstrated_result: The government-hosted Science and Technology Daily article, Xinhua Finance report and July Jiangsu government report are accessible and publish accounts of Yangzhou compute-electricity coordination activity, including an earlier pilot report. This establishes what publishers reported; it does not independently verify that the stages are one system, its dispatch behavior, commissioning chronology or outcomes.
technical.implementation_status: Secondary reports describe an existing pilot/operations-center stage in July, a September trial and citywide operation around Oct 27–28. A July provincial report names Yangzhou Big Data Group and State Grid Yangzhou in a completed compute-electricity pilot, while the Oct 29 government-hosted article says they jointly developed the city-level platform. The operator’s accessible Canal City compute marketplace page documents an existing compute-ordering and resource-aggregation service, but does not document the new electricity-coordination functionality or reconcile these stages.
technical.mechanism: The reports describe a platform connecting power-grid firms, compute providers and compute users. Price signals and hourly carbon-intensity data are used to advise or schedule flexible non-real-time workloads in lower-price or cleaner periods, with some jobs potentially routed to western regions with more renewable electricity. The published material does not specify dispatch authority, workload-selection rules, software architecture or the source and resolution of carbon accounting.
technical.regime: A Yangzhou city-level compute coordination platform reported to connect 24 resource pools totaling 16,000 PFLOPS and more than 5,000 registered users. Aggregate capacity is not effective training throughput; no accelerator mix, utilization or network information is given.
technical.reproducibility: No dispatch logs, public API, methodology, independent evaluation or reproducible workload comparison were located.
technical.strongest_baseline: No public task-level comparison, pricing schedule, transaction ledger, power/carbon methodology or matched operating baseline was available. Xinhua Finance's claimed same-task timing shift is a bounded scenario but its measurement protocol and denominator are not reported.

brief.title: Yangzhou reports a citywide platform coordinating compute with electricity price and carbon signals
brief.why_it_matters: If the platform operates as described, citywide coordination of flexible compute with grid prices and hourly carbon data could change how AI workloads are scheduled across data centers and how renewable electricity is absorbed. The reports describe a meaningful infrastructure implementation, but do not establish sustained cost or emissions benefits, transferability, or effects on AI compute availability.
